newsitem.title: USA: Economic adviser Tyson leaving White House.
newsitem.headline: Economic adviser Tyson leaving White House.

text.p: White House economic adviser Laura Tyson is leaving President Clinton's administration to teach at the University of California, her spokesman Christopher Dorval said.

"She's leaving, but she's willing to stay until the transition (to Clinton's second term) is complete," Dorval said, indicating Tyson would stay until January at the latest. Clinton will be inaugurated for his second term on Jan. 20.

Tyson, 49, has chaired Clinton's National Economic Council, which coordinates the administration's economic policies, for the last two years. Before that she chaired the president's Council of Economic Advisers, a small group of professional economists that make administration forecasts.

Dorval said Tyson was leaving the administration for family reasons. Her husband and son have already returned to California, where the family lived before coming to Washington after Clinton's 1992 election victory.
Dorval said Tyson had been asked if she would be interested in any other Cabinet posts, but she refused. "She shut down the discussion pretty quickly."
He said he did not know when her successor would be named or who it might be. "I presume whoever her successor is will work closely with her for a period of time."
In the meantime Tyson is working on "a series of transition items," Dorval said, including the possibility of forming commissions to work on the future of Medicare and Social Security.
